---

# Findings

## BLOCKER — none

Both files are faithful TypeScript conversions. All 18 enumerated Step 1 sites landed; all 5 Step 2 literals are correctly acknowledged; nothing outside the plan changed on disk.

**Verified measurements** (builder's figures reproduce exactly; the two measures differ, so state which):

| | hunks | `git diff --no-index --numstat` | GNU `diff -u` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `product-view` | **22** ✓ | **309** ✓ (203+106) | 299 |
| `product-detail` | **28** ✓ | **333** ✓ (224+109) | 325 |

Methodology check nobody was assigned: both files are **prettier-clean under `.prettierrc.yaml`** (`--check` exit 0), and installed `retail-react-app` is **10.0.0**, matching both headers and `package.json:23`. So the normalisation diff is a valid fidelity measure — it is not conflating formatting drift with real change.

---

## DEFECT 1 — Undocumented behaviour deviation: `ref?.scrollIntoView` — **CONFIRMED**

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:513`

```
base index.jsx:454   if (ref.scrollIntoView) {
ours  index.tsx:513   if (ref?.scrollIntoView) {
ours  index.tsx:514     ref.scrollIntoView({      ← note: NO `?.` here
```

There are exactly **five** `?.`/optional-call deviations from base across the two files. Four carry an explicit `// Deviation from the base file` comment (`product-view:359`, `product-view:632`, `product-detail:237`, `product-detail:608`). **This one has none** — the only comment in scope is base's own `// Get the reference to the product view and scroll to it.`

The asymmetry inside two adjacent lines is the tell: the guard got `?.`, the call on the next line did not. That is the signature of satisfying `strictNullChecks` on the guard (`ChildProductRef.ref` is typed `HTMLDivElement | null` at `:124`) and letting TypeScript's truthiness narrowing cover line 514 — not a considered defensiveness decision. Corroborating: the outer `childProductRefs.current[firstUnselectedProduct.id]` destructure on `:511` can be `undefined` and would throw, and is left unguarded in both files.

Real but narrow behaviour change: with `ref === null`, base throws a `TypeError` out of `handleChildProductValidation`; ours falls through to `return false`. **Fix either way** — revert to `ref.scrollIntoView` with a commented non-null assertion, or add the same two-line deviation comment the other four received.

## DEFECT 2 — `product-detail` header names a `console.log` marker that does not exist — **CONFIRMED**

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:13-15`

> "The only differences are the TypeScript annotations below, house formatting, and **the temporary override marker log**, which is removed once the override is confirmed to be rendering."

`grep -n "console\."` returns **zero hits in both files** (and zero in both base files — no fidelity deviation either direction). The marker was correctly removed per AGENTS.md's copy-first step 4; the sentence describing it was not. A reviewer will hunt for a log that isn't there.

## DEFECT 3 — Both port headers over-claim "behaviour unchanged", contradicting their own in-file deviation comments — **CONFIRMED**

- `product-detail/index.tsx:13` — "The only differences are the TypeScript annotations below, house formatting, and the marker log." Omits the three `?.` deviations *and* the relative `ProductView` import, which changes **which component renders**.
- `product-view/index.tsx:13` — "Behaviour is deliberately unchanged from the base file", contradicted by its own `:359` and `:632` "Deviation from the base file" comments.

This matters more than a normal stale comment: the header **is** this commit's audit trail, and "faithful port, nothing more" is its entire premise.

## DEFECT 4 — Operational: a bare `git commit` ships all 29 staged files under a copy-first message — **CONFIRMED (index state)**

The index holds 29 files. Post-Step-1, `ZimmProductContent`/`ModelInfo`/`StyleCode`/`Name`/`Price`/`Description` and `productInfo.ts` have **zero live consumers**, and `theme/components/index.ts:13-16,31-34` registers four recipes nothing renders. The plan settles this (files stay on disk; each commit selects **by path**), so it is not a code defect — but no gate catches it, and the commit command is the single remaining way COMMIT 1 goes wrong. COMMIT 1's correct path set is the two ports + `routes.tsx` + `vendor.d.ts`.

**Static import-closure check confirms that set is self-consistent standalone**: `product-view` imports only `node_modules`; `product-detail`'s sole relative import is `'../../components/product-view'` (in the set); `routes.tsx` adds the `/product/:productId` entry; `vendor.d.ts` supplies the `react-helmet` and `pwa-kit-react-sdk/ssr/universal/errors` declarations `product-detail` needs. Nothing else in the set imports an uncommitted path.

**Subtle consequence — PLAUSIBLE:** `scripts/hooks/pre-commit` `git add`s `.claude/registry/` *and* `.cursor/rules/`, `.vscode/instructions/`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md` (`:85`). Under a partial commit (`git commit <paths>`), git builds a temp index from HEAD + the named paths, so hook-staged changes to unnamed paths are generally **not** included. If so, the plan's expectation that COMMIT 1 rewrites `.claude/registry/components.md:54` will not hold, and the registry churn stays staged for a later commit. I could not prove this without mutating git state. Commit subject `refactor(product-view): copy-first TypeScript port of product-view and product-detail` **passes** `commit-msg:17`'s pattern (60-char description, valid scope).
